name: ACE (Agentic Context Engineering)
authors_affiliation: Qizheng Zhang, Changran Hu, Shubhangi Upasani, Boyuan Ma, Fenglu Hong, Vamsidhar Kamanuru, Jay Rainton, Chen Wu, Mengmeng Ji, Hanchen Li, Urmish Thakker, James Zou, Kunle Olukotun. Affiliations: Stanford University (Zhang, Zou, Olukotun), SambaNova Systems Inc. (Hu, Upasani, Ma, Hong, Kamanuru, Rainton, Wu, Ji, Thakker), UC Berkeley (Li). Equal contribution: Qizheng Zhang and Changran Hu.
task_domain: Agentic / interactive agents (tool-use, API understanding, code generation, environment interaction) and domain-specific reasoning (financial analysis, plus medical reasoning and text-to-SQL). Spans agent and domain-specific reasoning rather than open-domain QA.
problem_setting: Context adaptation: improving LLM behaviour by modifying the input context (system prompts, agent memory, evidence) rather than updating model weights. Studied in two modes: offline adaptation (optimize a system prompt / playbook on a training split, then evaluate on a test split with pass@1) and online adaptation (evolve agent memory at test time as samples stream in). Single LLM is used for all three roles (Generator/Reflector/Curator) to avoid knowledge transfer. Adaptation can use ground-truth labels OR rely solely on natural execution feedback (e.g. code execution success/failure), making it work with and without labeled supervision. Single-agent private context; not multi-agent shared memory.
what_is_retrieved: Structured, itemized 'bullets' from an evolving context 'playbook': reusable strategies/insights, domain concepts, formulas/calculations, tool-use guidelines, and common failure modes (mistakes to avoid), each tagged with helpful/harmful counters. The entire curated playbook is loaded into context (rather than top-k retrieved per query).
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic memory the agent writes and curates online (an evolving playbook). Built from the agent's own execution traces; not a static external document/KB corpus. Offline-warmup can initialize it, but it grows during deployment, so effectively growing-memory (HYBRID offline-init + online-growth).
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Not a fixed top-k ranking objective. ACE deliberately accumulates a comprehensive, detailed playbook (the whole curated context is injected, capped by a token budget) to preserve complete domain knowledge and avoid brevity bias / context collapse, prioritizing completeness and detail over concise selection.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Realizes CBR-like phases under different naming (not explicitly framed as CBR): Retrieve (whole playbook loaded into Generator context) / Reuse (Generator applies bulleted strategies) / Revise (Reflector distills corrective insights from successes/errors) / Retain (Curator merges delta bullets, grow-and-refine prunes/dedups). All four flags present in spirit. [uncertain on strict CBR mapping]
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself as 'context adaptation' / 'agentic context engineering' and 'evolving playbooks', inspired by Dynamic Cheatsheet and LLM memory frameworks (A-MEM). It does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner or claim case-based reasoning.
retrieval_unit: guideline-rule / strategy bullet (a 'bullet' = small itemized unit such as a reusable strategy, domain concept, formula, or common failure mode, plus metadata: unique ID + helpful/harmful counters). Conceptually similar to a memory entry in Dynamic Cheatsheet / A-MEM.
index_source: Growing memory induced online/at test-time from the agent's execution traces; can be offline-induced via offline warmup on a training split, then continues to grow online. Hybrid offline-init + online/test-time-induced.
index_structure_topology: Sectioned / category-keyed itemized list (a structured playbook with labeled sections such as STRATEGIES & INSIGHTS, FORMULAS & CALCULATIONS, COMMON MISTAKES TO AVOID), each holding ID-tagged bullets with helpful/harmful counters. Not a vector index or knowledge graph; effectively a hierarchical (section -> bullet) structured store. A de-dup step compares bullets via semantic embeddings.
retriever_type: LLM-as-context-manager / no learned dense retriever in the classic sense. The full playbook is supplied to the Generator; the Generator itself flags which bullets were useful or misleading. De-duplication uses semantic embeddings for similarity comparison during grow-and-refine.
retriever_learning_signal: None for a trained retriever (off-the-shelf). Bullet utility is tracked via non-learned helpful/harmful counters updated by the Reflector from execution feedback; selection/curation is driven by LM-feedback (Reflector insights) and natural execution outcomes rather than a contrastively trained or RL-trained retriever.
query_construction: No explicit query is formed for retrieval; the whole curated playbook is injected as part of the Generator's input context. The Generator, while solving a new query, marks which bullets were helpful/misleading, which provides the feedback signal for the Reflector. Effectively task/query-conditioned usage of a global context rather than per-query retrieval.
query_granularity: Task-level: the playbook is provided as context for each task/query (one shared evolving context), with adaptation done per-sample (batch size 1) to construct delta updates.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot per task for usage (whole playbook injected at the start of solving a query). Adaptation/update is iterative across samples (online) or epochs (offline).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule for context injection (playbook always provided to Generator). For updates, the trigger is execution/reflection-based: after the Generator produces a trajectory, the Reflector critiques it (using execution feedback such as code success/failure, or GT labels when available) and proposes corrective delta bullets that the Curator merges.
reranking: No retrieval reranking stage. Instead, a grow-and-refine de-duplication/pruning step periodically (proactively after each delta, or lazily when the context window/token budget is exceeded) prunes redundant bullets via semantic-embedding similarity.
retrieved_context_refinement: Curation/refinement of the context store: Reflector distills concrete insights from successes/errors (optionally across multiple refinement rounds, default up to 5); Curator merges compact delta bullets via deterministic, non-LLM logic; grow-and-refine performs de-duplication, pruning, and in-place counter updates, capped by a playbook token budget.
tool_document_engineering: N/A. ACE does not engineer tool/API descriptions for indexing; the AppWorld setting uses the official ReAct tool interface. Bullets may contain tool-use guidelines and readily-usable code snippets, but these are curated from execution traces, not from tool docstrings.
index_content_separation: N/A / partial. There is no lightweight-index-then-load-content split; the curated playbook itself (with section headers and ID-tagged bullets) is the content loaded into context. Metadata (IDs, helpful/harmful counters) is lightweight, but heavy content is not separately deferred.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A. Tool integration follows the AppWorld official ReAct implementation; ACE does not introduce a live-synchronized tool index, RapidAPI/MCP/function-calling protocol, or CRUD auto-sync of a tool store.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A. ACE does not model inter-tool dependency graphs; tool-use knowledge is captured implicitly as free-text strategy/failure-mode bullets in the playbook.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the evolved playbook (curated strategies, formulas, failure modes) is injected into the Generator's input context as a comprehensive system prompt / agent memory, guiding reasoning and tool use. No weight updates.
planning_integration: One-shot context injection at plan/act time: the playbook conditions the ReAct agent's multi-turn reasoning and tool use. The playbook is updated between episodes/samples (online) or epochs (offline) rather than inside a tree/MCTS search. Effectively retrieve(load playbook)-then-plan/act, with the playbook itself evolving from execution feedback.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-task / per-episode: the whole playbook conditions an entire ReAct rollout. Updates are per-sample (a delta context distilled from each sample); not per-CoT-step or per-token interleaving.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted, execution-feedback-driven revision: the Reflector distills corrective insights from successes/errors (optionally iteratively refined), and the Curator integrates them as localized delta-bullet edits merged by deterministic non-LLM logic. Bullets are reused largely verbatim as in-context guidance; revision happens at the playbook level rather than per-case adaptation. [uncertain whether this counts as classic CBR case adaptation]
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled strategy / structured note: free-text itemized bullets (strategies, domain concepts, formulas, common mistakes) tagged with IDs and helpful/harmful counters, sometimes including readily-usable code/tools; organized into a structured playbook. Not raw trajectories or latent tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled strategy/insight and state-aware guideline/rule (reusable heuristics, domain concepts, formulas, common failure modes) abstracted from raw trajectories; more abstract than a raw trajectory but more detailed/comprehensive than a terse summary.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Reflector-based self-reflection separates evaluation/insight extraction from curation; helpful/harmful counters and grow-and-refine de-duplication/pruning limit redundancy and harmful bullets; ACE is shown robust to weak/noisy reflectors and degrades gracefully (staying above base model except under fully adversarial updates every iteration). Effectiveness still depends on feedback quality (degrades without reliable GT/execution signals).
memory_type: Workflow/procedural playbook memory (structured, itemized strategy store) functioning as agent memory; non-parametric, append-and-refine. Closest to skill-library/workflow + episodic-insight memory.
write_back: True. The system stores new experiences/insights as delta bullets into the playbook: Curator integrates Reflector-distilled lessons, appending new-ID bullets and updating existing ones in place.
online_growth: Yes. In online adaptation the playbook grows during deployment/test-time as samples stream in; offline warmup can pre-populate it, but it continues to expand and refine online (grow-and-refine).
write_back_trigger: Reflective (after self-critique): each sample's Generator trajectory is critiqued by the Reflector (using execution feedback and/or GT labels), and the Curator writes delta bullets. Triggered on both successes and failures (the Reflector distills insights from successes and errors), batch size 1, optionally over multiple epochs offline.
failure_experience_usage: Both success and failure are used: the Reflector distills concrete insights from successes AND errors; bullets include 'common mistakes to avoid' (failure-mode/corrective rules), and helpful/harmful counters track which bullets help vs. mislead. Not success-only.
memory_evolution_update: Delta-update + dedup-merge + forget-prune + link-and-evolve: incremental delta updates (localized bullet edits) instead of monolithic rewrite; new-ID bullets appended, existing bullets updated in place (e.g. incrementing counters); grow-and-refine performs semantic-embedding de-duplication and pruning (proactive or lazy when token budget exceeded). Explicitly avoids full-context rewriting to prevent context collapse.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Context curation is not an RL/learned policy; it is LLM-prompted reflection + deterministic non-LLM merging with counter-based heuristics and embedding de-duplication. (Paper notes GEPA's RL comparison, but ACE itself is not RL-trained.)
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Single-agent private context in the reported experiments (one evolving playbook per task, with one LLM serving Generator/Reflector/Curator). No explicit cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing; playbooks are model-agnostic and portable across LLM backbones, but sharing across multiple agents is not a focus. [uncertain]
benchmarks: AppWorld (agent benchmark: API understanding, code generation, environment interaction; test-normal and test-challenge splits); FiNER and Formula/XBRL-Formula (financial analysis over XBRL; from FinLoRA/loukas2022finer & wang2025finlora); plus additional domain tasks from StreamBench: DDXPlus (medical reasoning) and BIRD-SQL (text-to-SQL).
benchmark_family: Web/agent (AppWorld) + tool/code/environment-interaction; domain reasoning: finance (FiNER, Formula), medical (DDXPlus), text-to-SQL (BIRD-SQL). Mix of agent (AppWorld) and domain-specific reasoning families.
baselines: Base LLM (no context engineering / default prompts); In-Context Learning (ICL, few/many-shot, agarwal2024many); MIPROv2 (DSPy prompt optimizer, auto='heavy'); GEPA (Genetic-Pareto reflective prompt optimizer, DSPy, auto='heavy'); Dynamic Cheatsheet (DC, online test-time memory, CU variant). For AppWorld all methods are built on the official ReAct implementation. Contextual leaderboard reference: IBM CUGA (GPT-4.1, top-1 production agent) - cited as contextual reference, not a methodological baseline.
key_metrics: AppWorld: Task Goal Completion (TGC) and Scenario Goal Completion (SGC) on test-normal and test-challenge, plus average; pass@1 in offline. FiNER/Formula/DDXPlus: accuracy (exact-match). BIRD-SQL: LLM-as-a-judge (GPT-4o-mini). Efficiency: adaptation latency, number of rollouts, token dollar cost (ingestion/generation).
headline_result: On AppWorld (DeepSeek-V3.1-671B base), ReAct+ACE reaches 59.4% average (+17.0 over ReAct's 42.4) offline with GT labels, matching the top-ranked production agent IBM CUGA (60.3%, GPT-4.1) and surpassing it on test-challenge with online adaptation; +10.6% average over selected baselines on agents and +8.6% on finance. Online without GT labels ACE improves AppWorld up to +17.1%.
ablations: Ablation on AppWorld (Table 3) over three factors: (1) Reflector with iterative refinement (ACE's addition beyond Dynamic Cheatsheet), (2) multi-epoch adaptation, (3) offline warmup. ReAct + ACE without Reflector or multi-epoch already gives +12.7 average (55.1 vs 42.4); adding each component yields further gains, confirming all are key. Additional studies: incremental context update (Appendix A.5, shown to be the key enabler vs monolithic rewrite that causes context collapse), robustness to reflection quality (Appendix A.4: robust to weak/noisy reflectors), hyperparameter sensitivity (Appendix A.6).
evaluation_decoupling: No separate intrinsic retrieval metrics (no Recall@k/nDCG): there is no top-k retrieval to score. Evaluation reports end-to-end task metrics (TGC/SGC/accuracy) plus efficiency metrics; context-collapse case study reports token count vs accuracy over adaptation steps.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (task/scenario goal completion, accuracy). Process is examined qualitatively via the context-collapse case study (token count vs accuracy per adaptation step) and ablations, but not via formal step-wise faithfulness/process scores.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: ACE substantially cheaper than adaptive baselines: offline AppWorld -82.3% adaptation latency and -75.1% rollouts vs GEPA (and -80.8%/-83.6% input/output token usage vs GEPA in offline adaptation); online FiNER -91.5% adaptation latency and -83.6% token dollar cost vs Dynamic Cheatsheet; ~86.9% lower adaptation latency on average vs existing adaptive methods (per repo). At eval time ACE uses more raw input tokens (richer playbook) but billed cost is mitigated by KV caching reuse.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Budget-capped: whole curated playbook injected, capped by a playbook token budget (default 80,000 tokens in the released code). Grow-and-refine prunes/dedups to stay within budget (proactively or lazily when window exceeded). No fixed top-k selection; budget + de-duplication govern size. Reflector refinement rounds and offline epochs default to 5 in the paper (repo defaults: max_num_rounds=3, num_epochs=1).
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (not a survey; ACE is a method paper).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark paper). Uses existing benchmarks; notes AppWorld difficulty: at submission the best leaderboard system achieved only 60.3% average accuracy. FiNER labels tokens with one of 139 fine-grained XBRL entity types; Formula tests numerical financial reasoning.
builds_on: Dynamic Cheatsheet (suzgun2025dynamic) - agentic test-time external-memory design ACE is directly inspired by; ReAct (yao2023react) - base agent loop; LLM memory frameworks like A-MEM (xu2025mem) for the memory-entry/bullet concept; DSPy ecosystem (MIPROv2, GEPA) for prompt-optimization baselines; long-context LLMs (DeepSeek-V3.1) for scaling comprehensive contexts.
contrasts_with: Monolithic-rewrite context optimizers and concise prompt optimizers: GEPA (brevity-as-strength reflective prompt evolution), MIPROv2 (Bayesian prompt optimization), ICL (fixed demonstrations), and Dynamic Cheatsheet's full-rewrite memory (which can cause context collapse). ACE contrasts by using structured incremental delta updates + grow-and-refine to avoid brevity bias and context collapse, and by adapting weights-free without labeled supervision via execution feedback.
lineage: Group F (decision/memory/RL) - self-improving LLM agents via evolving non-parametric memory/context. Sits in the test-time context-adaptation / agent-memory lineage (Dynamic Cheatsheet, Reflexion, GEPA, TextGrad), extending memory frameworks (A-MEM) toward structured, incrementally-updated 'playbook' memory for self-improving agents.
